title: Protective effect of scorpion-venom heat-resistant peptide (SVHRSP) against depression associated with Parkinson's disease via suppression of CREB-Akt pathway-mediated inflammation.
authors: Iqbal, Muhammad Khalid; Supratik, Kundu; Khan, Bakhtawar; Ahmad, Kabir; Ge, Yuxuan; Ai, Yu; Shaikh, Salman; Khalil, Muhammad Ibrahim; Guo, Song-Yu; Sui, Ao-Ran; Zhao, Yi-Fan; Li, Qi-Fa; Wang, Bin; Zhao, Chun-Li; Li, Shao
one_liner_zh: 该文研究蝎毒耐热肽对帕金森病伴抑郁的神经保护作用，涉及CREB-Akt通路和分子对接，但核心是疾病表型与信号通路，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，仅分子对接为边缘方法。
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Parkinson's disease (PD), characterized by motor dysfunction and dopaminergic neuron loss in the substantia nigra, is frequently complicated by depression (depression-associated PD, DPD), affecting 40-50% of patients and accelerating disease progression. This study investigated neuroprotective effects in a chronic MPTP-induced mouse model of DPD. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: We established a chronic PD model induced by MPTP, with motor deficits assessed via rotarod and gait analysis. Depressive phenotypes were confirmed by tail suspension, sucrose preference and forced swim tests. Mice were categorized into DPD and non-depressive groups, followed by 14-day treatment with SVHRSP or vehicle. KEY RESULTS: Post-treatment behavioural evaluations demonstrated that SVHRSP significantly ameliorated depressive symptoms, as evidenced by increased sucrose preference, reduced immobility in the forced swim test and restored cognitive performance in the Y-maze, passive-avoidance and novel-object-recognition tests. Molecular analyses demonstrated that SVHRSP enhanced neuroprotection by normalizing the phosphorylated Akt and CREB levels, reducing neuroinflammatory markers (IBA1, GFAP and cytokines) and modulating synaptic proteins (NR2B and PSD-95). Immunofluorescence further corroborated these findings, confirming reduced NR2B and NR1 expression and preserved neuronal integrity. SVHRSP downregulated Nav1.6 ion channel expression and restored 5-HT(2C) receptor levels and normalized stress-axis glucocorticoid receptor (GR) expression. Molecular docking simulations revealed strong binding affinities between SVHRSP and CREB/Akt. CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: The results indicate that SVHRSP mitigates motor deficits, depressive symptoms and cognitive impairments in MPTP-induced DPD mice by suppressing CREB-Akt-mediated neuroinflammation and modulating synaptic plasticity. The multitarget mechanism of SVHRSP underscores its potential as a novel therapeutic candidate for DPD.
abstract_zh: 背景与目的：帕金森病（Parkinson's disease, PD）以运动功能障碍和黑质多巴胺能神经元丢失为特征，常并发抑郁（抑郁相关帕金森病，DPD），影响40-50%的患者并加速疾病进展。本研究在慢性MPTP诱导的DPD小鼠模型中探讨了神经保护作用。实验方法：我们建立了MPTP诱导的慢性PD模型，通过转棒实验和步态分析评估运动缺陷。抑郁表型通过悬尾实验、糖水偏好实验和强迫游泳实验确认。小鼠被分为DPD组和非抑郁组，随后接受SVHRSP或载体治疗14天。主要结果：治疗后行为评估显示，SVHRSP显著改善抑郁症状，表现为糖水偏好增加、强迫游泳实验中不动时间减少，以及Y迷宫、被动回避和新物体识别实验中认知功能恢复。分子分析表明，SVHRSP通过恢复磷酸化Akt和CREB水平、减少神经炎症标志物（IBA1、GFAP和细胞因子）以及调节突触蛋白（NR2B和PSD-95）来增强神经保护。免疫荧光进一步证实了这些发现，确认NR2B和NR1表达降低且神经元完整性得以保留。SVHRSP下调Nav1.6离子通道表达，恢复5-HT(2C)受体水平，并正常化应激轴糖皮质激素受体（GR）表达。分子对接模拟揭示了SVHRSP与CREB/Akt之间的强结合亲和力。结论与意义：结果表明，SVHRSP通过抑制CREB-Akt介导的神经炎症和调节突触可塑性，减轻MPTP诱导的DPD小鼠的运动缺陷、抑郁症状和认知障碍。SVHRSP的多靶点机制凸显其作为DPD新型治疗候选药物的潜力。
